growth_thesis.claim: Lindblad segment growth has been driven by higher occupancy, guest nights sold, and pricing, with segment tour revenues rising 17% to $495.6 million in 2025 and 11% to $153.4 million in the third quarter of 2026.
quotes: Tour revenues for the year ended December 31, 2025 increased $72.3 million, or 17%, to $495.6 million compared to $423.3 million for the year ended December 31, 2024.

Lindblad segment tour revenues of $153.4 million increased $15.8 million, or 11%, compared to the third quarter a year ago primarily due to an increase in occupancy to 91% on a 4% increase in available guest nights, driving a 6% increase in net yield to $1,398.

growth_thesis.claim: For Lindblad segment volume and yield growth to continue, discretionary travel demand must remain resilient to economic downturns, geopolitical disruptions, and industry capacity growth.
quotes: In particular, a deterioration in global economic conditions that adversely affects discretionary income and consumer confidence may, in turn, result in decreased bookings, prices and onboard revenues for the expedition and cruise industries.

The growth in capacity from these new ships and future orders, without an increase in the cruise industry’s share of the vacation market, could depress expedition prices and impede our ability to maintain high yields.

growth_thesis.claim: For marine expedition growth to continue, vessels must avoid extended unscheduled drydockings or mechanical failures and ports and remote destinations must remain accessible.
quotes: Any such delays, cancellations of expeditions and/or unscheduled drydockings could have a material adverse effect on our business, results of operations and financial condition.
Any limitations on the availability or feasibility of our ports of call or expedition destinations could adversely affect our results of operations.

growth_thesis.claim: Fleet expansion and charter optimization drive capacity growth, including the $16.0 million cash acquisition of Torcatt Enterprises in 2025 and planned 2027 deployments of the Greg Mortimer and chartered river ship Evolve.
quotes: On January 9, 2025, we completed the acquisition of Torcatt Enterprises Limitada, a holding company that owns and operates two vessels in the Galápagos Islands, for $16.0 million in cash.

In 2026, the Company is retiring its National Geographic Sea Bird and National Geographic Sea Lion vessels following their Alaska expedition season and will be sailing the Greg Mortimer for Alaska itineraries in 2027 through 2029.
For voyages beginning in 2027, we have added an additional charter vessel, the Evolve.

growth_thesis.claim: For fleet-driven growth to continue, the company must access sufficient liquidity on favorable terms and shipyards must complete builds, modifications, or repairs without major delays or cost overruns.
quotes: Our inability to access sufficient liquidity on favorable terms when needed would have a negative impact on our ability to expand our fleet, our results of operations and our financial condition.

Any significant delays, cost overruns or failure to timely deliver a new vessel or complete modifications or repairs on existing vessels we have committed to service our guests could adversely affect us in several ways, including delaying the implementation of our business strategies, materially increasing our cost of servicing our commitments to our guests or resulting in the cancellation of scheduled expeditions, which have occurred in the past.

growth_thesis.claim: Land Experiences growth is driven by additional trips, higher guest counts and pricing, and acquisitions such as Thomson Group, increasing segment tour revenues 24% to $275.4 million in 2025 and 13% to $115.8 million in the third quarter of 2026.
quotes: Tour revenues for the year ended December 31, 2025 increased $54.0 million, or 24%, to $275.4 million compared to $221.4 million in 2024, primarily due to operating additional trips, higher pricing, and inclusion of the full year of the results of Thomson Group, acquired in July 2024.
Land Experiences tour revenues of $115.8 million increased $13.2 million, or 13%, compared to the third quarter a year ago primarily due to an increase in guests and operating additional trips.

growth_thesis.claim: The September 2026 acquisition of a 60% controlling interest in White Desert and Echo Charlie for approximately $66.6 million expands the experiential travel platform into luxury Antarctic interior and aviation-based travel.
quotes: During September 2026, we acquired a 60% controlling interest in White Desert and Echo Charlie for an aggregate cash purchase price of approximately $66.6 million, subject to customary adjustments for working capital, cash and indebtedness.
The acquisition expands our experiential travel platform through the addition of Antarctic expedition and aviation-based travel offerings.

growth_thesis.claim: For acquisition-led and new-market growth to continue, acquired businesses must be integrated smoothly with aligned controls and realized synergies without impairing goodwill or intangible assets.
quotes: Accordingly, we cannot make any assurances that past or future acquisitions will be completed timely or at all or that, if completed, we would realize the anticipated benefits of such acquisition.

In addition, acquisitions may also adversely impact our liquidity and/or debt levels, and the recognized value of goodwill and other intangible assets can be negatively affected by unforeseen events and/or circumstances, which may result in an impairment charge.

growth_thesis.claim: For Natural Habitat's conservation travel growth within Land Experiences to continue, the license agreement with World Wildlife Fund through December 2028 must be maintained without material adverse modification or termination.
quotes: Natural Habitat partners with WWF to offer conservation travel through a license agreement that allows Natural Habitat to use the WWF name and logo in return for a royalty fee, through December 2028.
If Natural Habitat’s license agreement with WWF was terminated or modified in any material respect, our results of operations for the Land Experiences segment may be materially adversely affected.

growth_thesis.claim: The expanded National Geographic partnership through 2040 drives bookings and brand reach via co-branding on owned vessels, co-selling through National Geographic's travel division, and increased marketing investment.
quotes: In November 2023, this strategic partnership with National Geographic was expanded and extended through 2040.

This relationship includes co-selling, co-marketing and branding arrangements with National Geographic Partners, LLC (“National Geographic”) whereby our owned vessels carry the National Geographic name and National Geographic sells our expeditions through their internal travel divisions.

Selling and marketing expenses for the year ended December 31, 2025 increased $27.7 million, or 32%, to $114.7 million, compared to $87.0 million for the year ended December 31, 2024, primarily due to higher royalties associated with the National Geographic agreement and increased revenues driving higher commissions expense and increased marketing spend to support future growth.
